rationale: PY-31 — a lambda is a function scope in python and this analyzer publishes no symbol for one, so nothing inside it can be attributed. `uses` already declined every member read inside a lambda (a read needs a symbol to source from); `calls` did not, so a call inside a lambda sitting directly in a CLASS BODY or at MODULE scope was attributed to that class or that module. `ShareableList -> decode` is a false statement about a class: a class body does not call anything, and `ShareableList.decode` is not a thing a reader of the graph can go and look at. Same class as this lane's PY-4 (`"global"` as a scope) and PY-28 (a nested def as an edge source). Found by running the independent oracle over CPython's stdlib, which reported two UNEXPLAINED `calls` edges in `multiprocessing/shared_memory.py` — both lambda bodies in a class-level dict of lambdas. MEASURED over 678 real python files (python-codesql + CPython 3.10 stdlib): 113 call nodes and 98 attribute nodes sit inside a lambda body across 43 files. The `expect` rows are the other half of the rule and matter as much as the forbids: a lambda INSIDE a def is that def's business, and the calls contract has always attributed a nested body's calls to the enclosing function, so those edges must survive.

expectRelationships.note: a lambda inside a METHOD. The attribution is `build`, the nearest named scope — dropping this row is how a fix for the class-body case becomes a fix for lambdas generally.
`key=lambda item: item[0].lower()` — a leaf reduction of a subscript, the same allowlist every other call goes through

forbidRelationships.note: THE defect. The call is in a lambda in the class body of `Handlers`; `Handlers` did not call `decode` and `Handlers.decode` does not exist. Measured: 2 unexplained edges of this shape in multiprocessing/shared_memory.py, 113 sites across 43 of 678 corpus files.
the sibling lambda on the next line — two lambdas, one class, two false claims about the class
the module-scope instance of the same shape: the module scope is a real navigable name, and naming it as the caller of a lambda's body call is still a false claim
member reads inside a lambda were already declined before PY-31 — pinned so the calls fix cannot quietly widen the uses rule, which would be a different change with a different number behind it
